title: What training does Section 1557 require under 45 CFR 92.9?
description: Section 1557 staff training under 45 CFR 92.9: who counts as a relevant employee, deadlines, 3-year records, and the 2025 court vacatur, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: 45 CFR 92.9, part of the 2024 rule implementing Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, requires covered health programs to train relevant employees on their civil rights policies and procedures, train new relevant employees within a reasonable period, retrain after material policy changes, and keep completion records for at least three years. A federal court vacated the rule's gender identity provisions in October 2025, but the training requirement itself was not vacated and remains in force.
keyTakeaways: Covered entities are recipients of federal financial assistance from the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), HHS itself, and entities established under Title I of the Affordable Care Act.

Training covers the written policies and procedures required by 45 CFR 92.8: the nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, language access, effective communication for people with disabilities, and reasonable modifications.

Relevant employees include anyone who interacts with patients or the public, anyone making decisions that affect patients' care (including executive leadership and legal counsel), and billing and collections staff.
Completion must be documented contemporaneously and kept for at least three calendar years under 92.9(c).

On October 22, 2025, the court in Tennessee v. Kennedy vacated listed provisions to the extent they define sex discrimination to include gender identity. HHS's June 2, 2026 notice confirms the other provisions remain in force.
regulator: Office for Civil Rights (OCR), US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
appliesTo: Health programs and activities that receive federal financial assistance from HHS, directly or indirectly, such as hospitals, health systems, clinics and other providers receiving that assistance
Health programs and activities administered by HHS or by entities established under Title I of the Affordable Care Act
Relevant employees of those programs, including permanent and temporary staff

sections.heading: Which organizations must provide Section 1557 training?

blocks.text: The training duty applies to covered entities, which [45 CFR 92.4](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-92/subpart-A/section-92.4) defines as a recipient of federal financial assistance, HHS itself, and an entity established under Title I of the Affordable Care Act. Under 92.2, the rule applies to every health program or activity any part of which receives federal financial assistance from HHS, directly or indirectly.

Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age or disability in covered health programs. The 2024 implementing rule, published May 6, 2024, turned that prohibition into specific administrative duties: a coordinator, written policies, notices, and staff training. The rule does not apply to an employer's employment practices, including employee health benefits (92.2(b)). This page states the position as at November 2026.

Covered entities must train relevant employees on the civil rights policies and procedures required by 92.8, as necessary and appropriate for their functions. The training standard is at [45 CFR 92.9](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-92/subpart-A/section-92.9).

blocks.title: 45 CFR 92.9(a)
blocks.text: "A covered entity must train relevant employees of its health programs and activities on the civil rights policies and procedures required by § 92.8, as necessary and appropriate for the employees to carry out their functions within the covered entity consistent with the requirements of this part."

The policies in question, listed in [45 CFR 92.8](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-92/subpart-A/section-92.8), are the written nondiscrimination policy; grievance procedures (for entities with 15 or more employees); language access procedures, including how an employee identifies limited English proficiency and obtains a qualified interpreter or translator; effective communication procedures for people with disabilities; and reasonable modification procedures. Training therefore needs to be built on the entity's own procedures, not a generic civil rights overview.

sections.heading: Who counts as a relevant employee?

blocks.text: Relevant employees are defined by what they do, under 92.9(b)(4). The definition is broader than patient-facing clinical staff, and it explicitly reaches the executive team and billing staff.

blocks.text: The definition covers permanent and temporary employees. The Section 1557 Coordinator, required for entities with 15 or more employees under [45 CFR 92.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-92/subpart-A/section-92.7), is responsible for coordinating training of relevant employees and maintaining the documentation. A [role-based training](/glossary/role-based-training) approach fits the three categories well.

sections.heading: When is Section 1557 training due, and what records are needed?

blocks.text: Initial training for existing relevant employees was due shortly after the entity implemented its 92.8 policies, so for most covered entities that deadline has already passed. Paragraph 92.9(b)(1) says training must be given "as soon as possible, but no later than 30 days following" implementation of the policies, and "no later than 300 days following July 5, 2024." The effective date schedule in [45 CFR 92.1(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-92/subpart-A/section-92.1) lists 92.9 as due following implementation of the 92.8 policies and no later than one year of July 5, 2024. Either way, both dates fell in 2025.

Ongoing triggers are new relevant employees, within a reasonable period after joining, and relevant employees whose functions are affected by a material change in the 92.8 policies or any other civil rights policies, within a reasonable period after the change. Completion must be documented contemporaneously, in written or electronic form, and kept for no less than three calendar years under 92.9(c). For record design, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: What is the litigation status of the Section 1557 rule as at November 2026?

blocks.text: The training requirement is in force; only gender identity provisions have been vacated. On July 3, 2024, the US District Court for the Southern District of Mississippi preliminarily enjoined HHS from enforcing the rule's gender identity provisions. On October 22, 2025, in Tennessee v. Kennedy, No. 1:24-cv-161-LG-BWR, the same court issued a final judgment vacating listed provisions to the extent they expand Title IX's definition of sex discrimination to include gender identity discrimination.

blocks.title: HHS notice of vacatur, June 2, 2026 (91 FR 32887)
blocks.text: The vacated provisions include 45 CFR 92.101(a)(2)(iv), 92.206(b)(1) to (4), 92.207(b)(3) to (5), 92.8(b)(1), 92.10(a)(1)(i) and 92.208, each to the extent it relates to gender identity. HHS states that OCR and CMS "cannot and will not enforce the vacated provisions" and that "the other provisions of the Section 1557 Rule remain in force." Section 92.9 is not on the list.

In practice, training content built on the nondiscrimination policy in 92.8(b)(1) should be reviewed so it reflects the vacatur, while the duties to train, retrain and keep records continue. The printed eCFR text has not been edited to remove the vacated language, so the [HHS notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/02/2026-11015/notice-of-vacatur-regarding-certain-provisions-of-the-2024-nondiscrimination-in-health-programs-and) is the reference for what is enforceable. No proposed rule replacing the 2024 rule appeared in Federal Register search results for Section 1557 HHS documents through November 2026, but further litigation or rulemaking could change this, and this page tracks only the case HHS reported. Treat a policy revision prompted by the vacatur as a material change and retrain affected staff; see [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How can a covered entity evidence compliance with 92.9?

blocks.text: Link each 92.8 procedure to the roles that use it, a measurable outcome and the record OCR would expect in an investigation. The mapping below is illustrative.

Identifies a patient with limited English proficiency and obtains a qualified interpreter using the entity's procedure.
Scenario assessment tied to the current procedure version; completion within the onboarding period

Arranges an appropriate auxiliary aid or service, such as a qualified sign language interpreter, for a patient who needs one.

Routes a disability-related modification request through the defined process and timeline.
Case-based assessment; Coordinator review of a sample of requests

Describes what changed in a revised civil rights policy and how it affects their tasks.
Targeted retraining records for affected roles, dated after the change

blocks.text: For the general method, see [how to map training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each 92.8 procedure to the relevant employee categories, the learning outcomes and the assessment points, with version history on each policy. When a court decision or policy revision changes the content, the affected roles and modules can be identified from those links and retraining assigned with dated records. See how this works for [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Was the Section 1557 training requirement struck down?
faqs.a: No. The October 22, 2025 judgment in Tennessee v. Kennedy vacated listed provisions only to the extent they treat gender identity discrimination as sex discrimination. Section 92.9 was not among them, and HHS's June 2, 2026 notice states that the other provisions of the rule remain in force.

No. 45 CFR 92.9 requires initial training, training for new relevant employees within a reasonable period after joining, and retraining after material changes to civil rights policies. It does not set an annual refresher, though an entity may choose one as part of its compliance program.

faqs.q: Do small practices need a Section 1557 Coordinator?
faqs.a: The Coordinator requirement in 92.7 and the grievance procedure requirement in 92.8(c) apply to covered entities that employ 15 or more persons. The training duty in 92.9 has no employee threshold, so smaller covered entities must still train relevant employees and keep records.

faqs.q: How long must Section 1557 training records be kept?
faqs.a: At least three calendar years. 45 CFR 92.9(c) requires covered entities to contemporaneously document employees' completion of the training in written or electronic form and retain the documentation for no less than three calendar years.
